doubts.claim_under_doubt: AC #4 claims no-agent_id keys stay byte-identical to prior behavior, i.e. a plain top-level PostToolUse payload never carries agent_id.
doubts.disproof_attempt: Live capture confirmed agent_id present on a SUBAGENT payload, but nothing had confirmed genuine absence on a top-level payload before this review — a wrong assumption would silently disable the gate for the ordinary orchestrator path, since bloat_gate_on_stop.py structurally never sees agent_id. Resolved with evidence already on hand: the same live-capture session's own first captured line (a top-level Edit call, made before any subagent ran) has no agent_id key at all in the payload. Not a live defect.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: _encode_agent_component's strict-mode utf-8 encode never raises on adversarial agent_id input.
doubts.disproof_attempt: An unpaired surrogate code point would raise UnicodeEncodeError inside the per-character loop. Accepted, not fixed: both hooks fail open on any exception; agent_id is Claude-Code-internal, not attacker-controlled.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The two hooks' _session_id() delegating wrappers are adequately covered by tests.
doubts.disproof_attempt: They are exercised only via subprocess-based integration tests, which per this repo's known diff-coverage limitation may register as uncovered by a strict line-coverage gate despite being behaviorally proven. Accepted, not fixed: pre-existing, project-wide, already-known gate characteristic.
